source.paraphrase: Function size exceeds the selected limit.

invariants.why: Function size exceeds the selected limit.
invariants.fixHint: Extract a cohesive operation and preserve behavior with relevant tests.
invariants.avoid: Do not compress statements onto one line or split a single state machine into arbitrary fragments.

source.paraphrase: Function parameter count exceeds the selected limit.

invariants.why: Function parameter count exceeds the selected limit.
invariants.fixHint: Review whether the inputs describe a cohesive domain object.
invariants.avoid: Do not hide unrelated inputs in a generic options map; Python self/cls and variadic parameters count, Go receivers do not.

source.paraphrase: Control-flow nesting exceeds the selected limit.

invariants.why: Control-flow nesting exceeds the selected limit.
invariants.fixHint: Use an early return or name a cohesive inner operation.
invariants.avoid: Do not hide nesting in loops, switch/match branches or exception handlers.

source.paraphrase: Declared public-method count exceeds the selected limit.

invariants.why: Declared public-method count exceeds the selected limit.
invariants.fixHint: Separate cohesive responsibilities while preserving the public API.
invariants.avoid: Do not rename public methods to private to hide the count; decorated definitions count as declarations.

source.paraphrase: A bare except also catches process-control exceptions.

invariants.why: A bare except also catches process-control exceptions.
invariants.fixHint: Name the intended exception classes or document a deliberately broad boundary.
invariants.avoid: Do not swallow KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit during ordinary error handling.

source.paraphrase: Error handling is part of what a function does: a caught error is dealt with, or passed on with enough context to act on it, never silently dropped.

invariants.why: Catching Exception or BaseException and doing nothing hides failures that a narrower handler or a deliberate boundary would surface.
invariants.fixHint: Handle the error with a fallback, logging plus re-raise, or translation into a domain error; catch a specific type when the failure mode is known.
invariants.avoid: Do not replace the body with a comment or treat binding the exception as handling. Log-only and continue is a separate smell.

source.work: Python documentation, The Python Tutorial and Programming FAQ
source.paraphrase: A default value is evaluated only once, so a mutable default such as a list or dict is shared by every call. Use None and create the value inside the function.

invariants.why: Every call that relies on the default reads and changes the same list, dict or set, so state leaks from one call into the next.
invariants.fixHint: Default to None and create the value in the body: items = [] if items is None else items. Use field(default_factory=list) in a dataclass.
invariants.avoid: Do not hide the shared value behind list(), dict(), set() or a collections constructor. A deliberate shared cache keeps the FAQ's underscore name, such as _cache={}.

source.work: Python documentation, What's New In Python 3.8
source.paraphrase: Identity checks with is and is not against string or number literals can work by accident in CPython but are not guaranteed by the language; use == and != instead.

invariants.why: is compares object identity. Whether two equal numbers or strings are the same object is an interpreter detail, so the check can flip between runs, versions or values.
invariants.fixHint: Compare values with == or != . Keep is only for None, True, False and sentinel objects.
invariants.avoid: Do not wrap the literal in parentheses, negate it or move it to the left side; those are still literals.

source.work: PEP 8, Style Guide for Python Code
source.paraphrase: Wildcard imports should be avoided because they make it unclear which names are present in the namespace. Republishing an internal interface as a public API is the defensible exception.

invariants.why: A wildcard import hides where a name comes from and lets a later change in the imported module silently shadow local names.
invariants.fixHint: Import the names the module uses, or import the module and qualify its names.
invariants.avoid: Package __init__.py files that republish submodules are not checked. An accelerator-module fallback elsewhere needs a reviewed exclusion, not a copied name list.

source.paraphrase: assert (a, b) is an assertion of a tuple, which always evaluates to True.

invariants.why: A non-empty tuple is always truthy in Python. assert (x > 0, 'must be positive') never fails, disabling the assertion completely.
invariants.fixHint: Remove parentheses: write assert x > 0, 'must be positive'.
invariants.avoid: Do not enclose assert condition and error message inside parentheses or leave a trailing comma in assert (x,).

source.paraphrase: NotImplemented is a constant returned by rich comparisons; it should never be raised.

invariants.why: NotImplemented is not an Exception class. Raising it raises a TypeError at runtime when caught by an except clause expecting Exception.
invariants.fixHint: Use raise NotImplementedError() instead of raise NotImplemented.
invariants.avoid: Do not raise NotImplemented or NotImplemented() in abstract methods or stubs.
